name: Nethaniah
overview: Nethaniah was a male figure noted in Scripture as the father of Ishmael, who served as one of the captains of the Judean forces. His identity is primarily recognized through his paternal relationship and connection to military leadership during a critical period in Judah's history. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Nethaniah means 'YHWH has given,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning tied to God's provision. This proper name is recorded in 2 Kings 25:23 and is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a clear acknowledgment of divine blessing.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Nethaniah as the father of Ishmael, who was a captain among the Judean forces, and as the father of Elishama, his son mentioned explicitly in 2 Kings 25:25. Beyond these relationships, no additional family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Nethaniah's significance lies in his connection to the leadership of Judah during a tumultuous time, as his son Ishmael held a notable military position. This association places Nethaniah within the narrative of Judah's final days before exile, highlighting the roles of his family in the unfolding history of God's people. His name's meaning also underscores the theme of divine provision amid national crisis.
